svg.title: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate: every local MegaLinter task reads the settings file the project chose
svg.text: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate
Scenario: every local MegaLinter task reads the settings file the project chose

g.text: Given the project names its own MegaLinter settings file in
The project keeps its own MegaLinter settings in project/megalinter.yml. The toolbox does not
ship that file, so a framework update never touches it. It builds on the toolbox's own file,
.config/megalinter/config.yml, and keeps only ShellCheck, so that a run takes seconds.
The last line comes from .env.dist: TASK_MEGALINTER_CONFIG=project/megalinter.yml tells the
MegaLinter tasks which file to read.
Then task megalinter loads the project's settings file
task megalinter, the usual way to run MegaLinter on a machine, starts it in Docker, where the
project sits in /tmp/lint. MegaLinter's own [config] line names the file it loaded:
/tmp/lint/project/megalinter.yml, the project's file. The next line shows that file builds on
Only ShellCheck runs, as that file asks, and the task ends on "All files correctly linted
And task megalinter:pnpm:dlx loads the same settings file
task megalinter:pnpm:dlx starts MegaLinter another way: pnpm downloads mega-linter-runner,
and the runner starts MegaLinter's image. MegaLinter's [config] line names the same file, and
the same single check runs with the same verdict.
